issues.t: Throttle body failure causes limp mode or stalling
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power with a wrench light or check engine light, the car stuck at low speed ("failsafe" mode), stalling, surging at low speed, or an unsteady idle.
issues.why: Dirt and contamination on the electronic throttle body's internal motor contacts cause a bad connection. Ford ran Customer Satisfaction Program 13N03, which extended throttle body coverage to 10 years or 150,000 miles; that coverage has since run out for most cars.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. If power drops suddenly, get safely off the road. Have the codes read; a new throttle body is the usual fix, and cleaning only helps for a while.

issues.t: CVT slips, shudders or won't engage
issues.sym: The engine revs without the car speeding up, shuddering when pulling away, a grinding or whining noise, or the car won't move in Drive.
issues.why: Cars with the continuously variable transmission (CVT, used on all-wheel-drive and some front-drive models) suffer internal bearing and belt wear. Repairs are often major.
issues.next: Have the transmission codes and fluid checked right away. Ask about a used or remanufactured unit, and weigh the repair against the car's age and condition before committing.

issues.t: Six-speed automatic slips, clunks or lunges into gear
issues.sym: Slipping between gears (often 4th to 5th), harsh clunks or a thump when shifting, lunging into gear, or a jerk when backing up.
issues.why: The six-speed automatic on front-drive cars suffers valve body and internal wear. Software updates fixed some early shift complaints.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about transmission software updates first. If it slips, have a specialist check the valve body before a full rebuild.

issues.sym: The A/C blows warm, or blows cold only while driving and warm at stops, sometimes with noise from the compressor.
issues.why: The A/C compressor is the single most-reported repair on the Five Hundred, and many owners have replaced it more than once.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested and the compressor checked. Replace the drier and expansion valve with the compressor to avoid repeat failure.

issues.t: All-wheel-drive system stops working or makes noise
issues.sym: A grinding or whining from underneath, a clunk on turns, or the car no longer sending power to the rear wheels.
issues.why: The AWD power transfer unit and rear drive unit can wear out or leak.
issues.next: Have the AWD fluid levels and seals checked. Ask a shop to confirm which unit has failed before replacing parts.

issues.sym: Clunking when shifting or accelerating, extra vibration at idle, or the engine rocking visibly.
issues.why: Engine mounts and the anti-roll mount bracket crack or wear out, which is a frequent repair on these cars.
issues.next: Have a shop watch the engine move while shifting between Drive and Reverse. Replace the broken mount.

issues.t: EGR valve failure turns on the check engine light
issues.sym: Check engine light, rough idle or hesitation.
issues.why: The EGR valve and its vacuum lines and sensor fail or clog; some owners have replaced the valve twice.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the lines checked for water or cracks before buying parts. Use a quality replacement valve.

issues.sym: Gauges, the odometer or warning lights in the dash go dead, flicker or read wrong.
issues.why: Solder joints inside the instrument cluster crack. Ford issued a service bulletin (TSB 06-17-9) for this.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Have the cluster tested. A rebuilt cluster or solder repair service is an option besides a new one.

issues.sym: One heated seat no longer warms up.
issues.why: The heating element in the seat fails; some owners have replaced it more than once.
issues.next: Have the seat heater circuit checked; the element is replaced under the seat cover.

issues.sym: Pulling to one side, a burning smell from a wheel, vibration, or one brake pad wearing very fast.
issues.why: Brake calipers, especially at the rear, seize from corrosion.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected; replace the sticking caliper and its pads and rotor.

issues.t: Front end creaks or clunks over bumps
issues.sym: Creaking, dry grinding or clunking from the front when turning or going over bumps.
issues.why: Worn lower control arm bushings, sway bar links and tie rod ends.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected and get an alignment after repairs.

issues.t: Power steering pump leaks or whines
issues.sym: A whine when turning, fluid drips near the front of the engine, or stiff steering.
issues.why: The power steering pump and its hoses leak with age.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and have the leak traced. Don't run the pump dry.

issues.sym: An oil smell, smoke from the engine bay, or oil around the spark plug area that can cause misfires.
issues.why: The valve cover gaskets harden and leak oil.
issues.next: Have the gaskets replaced, and check the spark plug wells for oil.

issues.sym: Battery light, dim lights, or a dead battery.
issues.why: The alternator wears out.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested before replacing the battery.

issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that rises with speed.
issues.why: Front and rear wheel bearings wear out.
issues.next: Have a shop find which wheel is noisy and replace the hub.

issues.t: Paint and clearcoat peeling or blistering
issues.sym: The clearcoat flakes off the hood or roof, or paint bubbles and blisters.
issues.why: Paint and clearcoat failure reported by owners, mostly on the hood and top surfaces.
issues.next: Ask a Ford dealer whether any paint coverage applies. Otherwise, a body shop can refinish the panel.

issues.t: Water collects in the doors or leaks inside
issues.sym: Water sloshing inside the doors, wet carpets, or fogged windows.
issues.why: Door drain holes clog and seals leak.
issues.next: Clear the drain holes at the bottom of each door and have the door seals checked.

issues.t: Clicking from the heater and A/C system
issues.sym: Clicking behind the dash, or heat that only works at the highest setting.
issues.why: A blend door actuator with worn plastic gears.
issues.next: Have the actuator tested and replaced.

issues.sym: A door that doesn't latch firmly or pops open.
issues.why: The door latch pawl might not return to the latched position (recall 06V-383).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.

issues.sym: A rattling or banging noise from under the car, or a fuel smell or leak.
issues.why: A fuel tank strap could break and lead to a fuel leak (recall 05V-515).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.

issues.sym: A fuel smell or drips near the gas cap or rear wheel.
issues.why: The fuel tank filler could leak fuel (recall 11V-355).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.
